title: The Fourth, 2004
venue: Arthur's site (newspaper cadence: six dailies + a Sunday)
logline: The strip is in color now. The fireworks can be red. Wood draws them white anyway.

panels.composition: Tier 1: the dock, night, crowded, Sunday page, in color — the sky Prussian blue, the shack warm, the cups white. The fireworks: white. Deliberately. GULLY pouring. WOOD on the steps.

image.prompt: a crowded wooden dock at night in watercolor with a deep Prussian blue sky and warm lamplight from a shingle shack, fireworks bursting pure white, a young man in an apron pouring coffee, another on the steps with a small dog
image.notes: Color everywhere except the fireworks. That's the strip's joke on itself.

panels.name: White

panels.composition: Tier 2: Gully on the steps for his one minute. Looking up.

balloons.text: They were white in mine. I'm not changing history.

image.prompt: two young men on shack steps at night looking up, watercolor, fireworks light

panels.name: History

panels.composition: Tier 3: the lawn chair under the eave, in color for the first time: faded green webbing, rust on the frame.

image.prompt: close-up of an old folding lawn chair with faded green webbing and a rusted frame under a shingle eave at night, watercolor

panels.name: The chair

panels.composition: Tier 4: the finale. White on blue. The dock. The chair. The two on the steps. The one red thing in the panel: a child's balloon, far end of the dock.

image.prompt: a fireworks finale in pure white over a Prussian blue night sky above a crowded dock, and one small red balloon at the far end of the dock, watercolor, no words
image.notes: The single red balloon: the only concession. It's a child's.

panels.name: One red thing

art.palette: Prussian blue, warm lamp yellow, white; one red

notes: The first Fourth in color. The fireworks stay white. One red balloon.
